newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan plastics rise on rebounding product prices.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan plastics rise on rebounding product prices.

text.p: Shares in Taiwan's plastics sector surged in early Monday trade on a recent rebound in raw material prices and rising demand from mainland China, brokers said.
After 55 minutes, plastics shares had surged 2.07 percent while the overall index was up 0.93 percent.

China Petrochemical was up T$1.5 or 3.89 percent to T$40.1 while Grand Petrochemical had surged T$1.7 or 5.81 percent to T$31. The shares were two of the top three most heavily traded shares in early trading.
Brokers noted recent price rebounds in various petrochemical raw materials such as styrene monomer and polyethylene.
Brokers said the price rebound was likely to be short-term.

"This should be a seasonal rebound (for petrochemical raw material prices) but they likely will fall again in the second quarter on expected oversupply due to rising new production capacity," said Nikko Securities research chief Michael Hung.
The plastics shares would be also be boosted by recent rising demand from mainland China, he said.
Brokers said plastics likely would emerge as a bellwether sector to lead overall upward momentum in the near term.
